metaData.originalTitle: Airbnb CEO：Airbnb 正在为 Agent 时代重做自己丨 Invest Like The Best
metaData.title: Airbnb CEO: Airbnb Is Reinventing Itself for the Agent Era | Invest Like The Best
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: In a podcast interview, Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky shares how the company is reinventing itself for the Agent era, from Founder Mode and the consumer AI renaissance to a strategic shift that redefines the core atomic unit from "homes" to "people."
metaData.summary: This article is a deep dive and summary of the podcast "Invest Like The Best" featuring Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky. Drawing from his background in industrial design, Chesky discusses his counterintuitive CEO management philosophy, including entering Founder Mode after the pandemic—a style of gaining deep control by mastering details before gradually delegating. He predicts that the next 12 to 24 months will mark the beginning of a consumer AI renaissance, arguing that AI should not be reduced to a chat box in old apps but will fundamentally transform software interfaces and distribution. Chesky shares Airbnb's internal innovation method of forming small 10-12 person teams and narrowing problems down to a manageable scale (e.g., a single city or a single funnel), along with the famous "11-star experience" mental model. He outlines Airbnb's next-decade strategy: shifting the atomic unit from "homes" to "people," building a community around user identity, preferences, and genuine relationships, rather than relying on the app format. Finally, he emphasizes that a CEO's most important job is hiring, and they should dedicate 50% of their time to it.

mainPoints.point: The CEO role is entirely counterintuitive and must be learned.
mainPoints.explanation: Chesky believes founders rely on intuition and conviction, while CEOs must balance diverse information and make difficult decisions. This ability cannot be improvised on the spot; it must be honed through a learning curve and crises, such as the pandemic.

mainPoints.point: The AI era will usher in a renaissance of consumer products.
mainPoints.explanation: Current AI is primarily enterprise-focused, but in the next 12 to 24 months, consumer AI will rise. The core of competition will no longer be model capability, but who can make tools simple enough and interfaces friendly enough for ordinary users to adopt.

mainPoints.point: For innovation in large companies, problems should be narrowed down to a sufficiently small scale.
mainPoints.explanation: Airbnb formed a small 10-12 person "Project Hawaii" team focused on the specific problem of improving user booking conversion rates. Starting with bug fixes and iterating gradually, they ultimately generated hundreds of millions of dollars in incremental revenue.

mainPoints.point: Airbnb's new atomic unit is "people," not "homes."
mainPoints.explanation: Chesky believes that in the Agent era, the app format may disappear. Airbnb's core asset should be a community built around user identity, preferences, and genuine relationships, not a list of listings.

mainPoints.point: A CEO's most important job is hiring, and they should dedicate 50% of their time to it.
mainPoints.explanation: Chesky considers not investing enough time in hiring early on as a "fatal mistake." He now spends 2-3 hours daily on hiring, building a long-term talent pipeline and tracing back from great work to find the people behind it, thereby reducing the cost of remedial management.

keyQuotes: No one is born a good CEO. The job is completely counterintuitive; almost every instinct will lead you astray.
We are in the enterprise AI phase. In the next 12 to 24 months, we will see the beginning of a consumer AI renaissance.
I don't want Airbnb to be just about homes. I want it to be about people.
The more time you spend on hiring, the less time you spend on managing.
Suddenly, each of us has a paintbrush and a canvas.
